children: Indonesia will maintain its half-half blend of palm-based diesel and conventional diesel next year, a senior energy ministry official said on Wednesday, with the take-up for the fuel known as B50 reaching 80% so far.
Indonesia started the implementation of B50 in July in an effort to reduce its reliance on imported fuel and contain rising energy costs caused by the war in the Middle East.
⁠"On average, (delivery) of B50 has reached 80%. We are still monitoring this month so that full B50 distribution can be met," senior energy ministry official Eniya Listiani Dewi told reporters.
Businesses were given until the end of September to clear out their B40 stock and transition into B50.
